neighbours.label: ' on' or ' upon' as the particle of 'take': taking on a role, a burden or a quality
fire: Our small firm decided to take on the new contract in May.
After the merger she took on extra duties at the bank.
The sauce will take on a smoky flavor as it cooks.
The young lawyer took on the case without any fee.
The volunteers took it upon themselves to clean the beach.
He is taking on the champion in next month's final.
In winter the hills take on a pale blue tint.
The charity has taken on the care of forty stray dogs.
quiet: Our small firm decided to rely on the new contract in May.
After the merger she worked on extra duties at the bank.
The sauce will take about an hour as it cooks.
The young lawyer took up the case without any fee.
The volunteers walked on the sand to clean the beach.
He is taking off for next month's final.
In winter the snow falls on the pale blue hills.
The charity has taken in forty stray dogs for care.

notes: ' on' is 29 of the top 32 peaks. Plain ' on' after other verbs stayed near zero in probes, so the word alone is not the label.
